audit_findings.title: Gross cash may double-count customer-funded deferred revenue
audit_findings.magnitude: $6,865.9 million deferred revenue ($5.34 per diluted share), equal to 51.5% of the $13,343.3 million cash bridge; $1,621.9 million of deferred cost of goods sold is separately recorded; actual overlap unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash and short-term investments while forecast OE may recognize revenue whose cash was collected before the valuation date, without deducting remaining performance costs or reversing the associated working-capital benefit.
audit_findings.evidence: Deferred revenue is comprised mainly of unearned revenue related to product deferrals from contracts with acceptance clauses and, annual and multi-year PCS contracts.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a deferred-revenue balance large enough to materially affect the bridge, but it does not demonstrate that all or any specified portion is collected cash included in the bridge. Thus double counting is unresolved rather than proven. The balance is sufficiently large relative to both cash and scenario equity values that a substantial overlap could materially lower intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile deferred revenue by product acceptance and PCS category to billings, cash collections, deferred costs, taxes, and remaining service costs; then rerun the bridge and forecast OE using either net excess cash or cash-flow-consistent deferred-revenue treatment.

audit_findings.title: Every scenario may understate the downside from extreme customer concentration
audit_findings.magnitude: 42% of FY2025 revenue, or $3,782.4 million computed from $9,005.7 million total revenue; OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A customer loss, purchasing reduction, discount, or product reallocation would reduce forecast revenue, margins, OE growth, and potentially inventory realizability; the current bear case stops at 0% growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Sales to one end customer represented 16 %, 15 % and 21 % of our total revenue, and sales to the other end customer represented 26 %, 20 % and 18 % of our total revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The 42% concentration is demonstrated, but no present customer loss or quantified reduction is established. This is therefore a forward-looking risk rather than a demonstrated error in the anchor. Its scale makes the absence of a negative-growth stress important, even though the existing record cannot quantify the probability or OE impact.
audit_findings.action: Rerun customer-specific stresses for partial and full reductions by each major customer, incorporating gross-margin discounts, fixed-cost deleverage, inventory charges, and any offsetting sales to other customers.

audit_findings.title: Cash classified as excess may be required to fund binding purchase obligations
audit_findings.magnitude: $9,700.0 million of June 2026 purchase commitments, including $9,400.0 million within 12 months, equal to 72.7% of the $13,343.3 million cash bridge; required liquidity offset unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash and short-term investments as distributable equity value even though some cash may be operating working capital needed to settle non-cancellable commitments before related inventory is sold and collected.
audit_findings.evidence: A significant portion of our purchase orders for finished goods and strategic components, including integrated circuits consigned to contract manufacturers, consists of non-cancellable commitments.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates legally binding commitments substantially larger than the earlier $6.8 billion finding and states that cash and securities support working capital. It does not establish that commitments should be deducted dollar-for-dollar because purchases create inventory and may be supported by customer demand. Nevertheless, treating every dollar of cash as excess without a liquidity reserve is reasonably capable of materially overstating the bridge.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile commitments to binding customer orders, deferred revenue, deposits, supplier payment dates, inventory conversion, customer collection terms, and downside cancellations; calculate a minimum operating-cash reserve and rerun all scenarios with only residual excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The OE numerator and bridge use different temporal acquisition perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: $300.0 million acquisition consideration; $116.4 million net tangible liabilities assumed; omitted full-year OE contribution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2025 anchor OE includes only post-June 30 results from VeloCloud, whereas June 2026 cash, liabilities, and shares reflect the combined company for the full balance-sheet perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: On June 30, 2025, we completed the acqu isition of the VeloCloud business ("VeloCloud") from Broadcom fo r total cash consideration of $ 300.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporal mismatch is demonstrated, but VeloCloud's standalone revenue, OE, integration costs, and assumed operating requirements are not disclosed. A profitable omitted half-year would understate value, while losses, integration costs, or incremental reinvestment could overstate it. The record therefore cannot establish direction or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Construct comparable full-perimeter FY2025 pro forma and latest-twelve-month OE from acquisition schedules or management data, including integration costs, acquired amortization treatment, working capital, and assumed liabilities, then rerun the valuation using the permitted anchor rule.

audit_findings.title: The anchor depends on unusually judgmental inventory and supplier-liability estimates
audit_findings.magnitude: $2,535.3 million June 2026 inventory; filed inventory charges were $131.6 million, $267.2 million, and $234.4 million for 2025-2023, a $211.1 million three-year average and $79.5 million above the 2025 charge; any additional deficiency unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Under-accrued inventory write-downs or supplier liabilities would overstate anchor OE and could also reduce excess cash through later settlement or inventory losses.
audit_findings.evidence: Auditing management’s assessment of net realizable value for inventory and supplier liability was complex and highly judgmental due to the assessment of management’s estimates of forecasted product demand, which can be impacted by changes in current and expected orders from customers, product development plans, and current sales levels.
audit_findings.explanation: Judgmental estimation is demonstrated, but neither the auditor's critical-audit-matter disclosure nor the charge history demonstrates an incorrect or optimistic reserve. The 2025 charge is already reflected in reported earnings. However, inventory rose to $2.535 billion and purchase commitments to $9.7 billion, so an undisclosed reserve deficiency could affect both OE and the cash bridge; its size cannot be established from the record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain June 2026 inventory aging, subsequent sales and cancellations, forecast-versus-actual demand, post-year-end provisions, and supplier-liability rollforwards; test the anchor against the filed three-year charge history and rerun only for evidenced reserve deficiencies or an explicitly approved normalization.

audit_findings.title: A non-debt tax claim may require an offset to gross cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $191.7 million gross unrecognized tax benefits, or $0.15 per diluted share; 1.4% of bridge cash and 0.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash-settleable tax obligation not already captured in forecast OE would reduce the excess-cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the total amount of gross unrecognized tax benefits was $ 191.7 million, $ 181.5 million and $ 163.3 million, respectively, of which $ 100.7 million, $ 103.4 million and $ 90.0 million would affect our effective tax rate if recognized.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes a $191.7 million gross uncertain-tax-position balance, not a presently payable claim of that amount. Even deducting the entire gross balance with no DTA, timing, or settlement adjustment would lower value by only about $0.15 per share, from $56.03 to approximately $55.88 in the base case. That scale is not material to the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the latest uncertain-tax-position balance, balance-sheet classification, expected cash settlement, and DTA or indemnity offsets; deduct only any independently payable amount not already reflected in forecast taxes.
